Hi Alex —

Thanks for the clear checklist. See answers below and attached evidence: SIG_BCDR_RTO_RPO_Answers_v2.pdf (consolidated table + commentary), network-diagram-region-overview.png (simplified public-facing diagram), backup-policy-2025.docx (internal policy excerpt).

1) RTO / RPO
- Production API (hosted): Contractual SLO for Dedicated customers is a 15-minute RTO for control plane incidents and 5-minute RTO for worker restarts with RPO of 1 minute for customer session state. For Hosted (multi-tenant) customers we publish an operational target (not contractual) of RTO 30 minutes and RPO 5 minutes. These are noted in the attached PDF with references to our SLA matrix.

2) Backups
- Metadata & config: snapshot every 15 minutes, retained for 30 days.
- Persistent model artifacts: nightly full backups, retained for 90 days by default with additional archival to cold storage for 1 year upon request.
- Backups are encrypted at rest using customer-managed KMS (if configured) or Redwood-managed KMS (AES-256) and encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+). Snapshot replicas are stored in a second region for Dedicated and Private customers; for Hosted customers cross-region replication is available as an opt-in addon.

3) Regional failover
- Dedicated & Private: we support automated failover for compute pools via our control-plane orchestrator. Failover includes route updates, cache rebuild orchestration, and service validation hooks. Expected automated failover window for a single-region outage: typically 6–12 minutes for traffic re-routing and worker provisioning; full KV cache warm-up depends on workload (additional minutes).
- Hosted: we have a runbook-based escalation with scripted steps for failover; manual operator approval required for cross-region DNS cutover. Typical runbook-based RTO for Hosted is up to 60 minutes depending on routing.

Attachments contain a short table that maps the above answers to SIG fields and includes further references to our DR runbook (internal link included).

Please confirm whether the attached package is sufficient or if you need an encrypted copy of the model artifact backup logs or a signed SOC/third-party attestation excerpt.

Best,

Alex —

Short answers below and I've uploaded a sanitized SOC excerpt and the updated diagram to the shared drive.

1) Cross-region backup encryption: Replicated snapshots are encrypted end-to-end. For customers using customer-managed KMS, we mirror encryption keys via key policies and CMK replication where supported; the snapshot remains encrypted with the same logical key material or wrapped key across regions. For Redwood-managed KMS, we re-encrypt with the regional KMS but maintain equivalent key strength (AES-256) and provide attestations in the SOC excerpt.

2) Hosted cross-region replication process & SLA: For Hosted customers who purchase the cross-region replication addon, we document the recovery process in the external-facing DR summary (uploaded). There is no separate SLA for cross-region replication for multi-tenant Hosted customers; the recovery process is runbook-driven and supported by our operations team. Dedicated customers have an optional SLA addendum that codifies a RTO window and automated failover behavior.

Links & attachments: sanitized SOC excerpt (drive link), updated network-diagram-region-overview.png (drive). Let me know if you need anything redacted further.
